bullets.title: DELL: Blowout Q3 — $132B AI Backlog, FY27 Guidance to $202B; Stock -5% on Margin Step-Down
bullets.body: Dell posted Q3 revenue of $54.94B (+103% y/y, vs. $49.32B consensus) and EPS of $9.45 vs. $6.60 consensus; ISG revenue surged +198% y/y with AI server revenue of $22B. FY27 guidance raised to $202B revenue and $29.68 EPS; $25B buyback added. Stock off ~5% pre-market on sequential ISG margin step-down expected in Q4 and modest AI server raise ($74B→$78B). Sell-side avg PT ~$522 (Citi $550, GS $510, Mizuho $500 cut from $650, Piper $555); 71% Buy.

bullets.title: NVDA: Down ~5-7% Pre-Market — Jensen Bounce Fades, Credit/Circular-Financing Concerns Persist
bullets.body: NVDA fell 5-7% in pre-market as the Jensen Huang reinstatement rally reversed. Key overhangs: CoreWeave bonds at record lows signaling circular-financing risk, California AG says reinstatement changes nothing for criminal probe, BIS GPU restrictions still contentious, and AI capex durability questioned. JPM notes BIS impact on SE Asia supply chain should be minimal and that 20-25% Asia Tech rally possible if EPS cuts don't materialize in 2-3 months; GS says sector needs better rates, credit, and Q4 AI revenue proof for re-rating.

bullets.title: Broad Semis/AI Basket Carnage: SOX -8%, AI Basket -6.4%, Global Chip Stocks Crushed
bullets.body: Pre-market semiconductor selloff is severe: MU -6.7%, AMD -5.8%, SNDK -6.8%, LITE/STX/CIEN -6%, ANET/VRT -4.5-5.6%, CRWV -6.8%, HPE -16% (worst since 2020) on Cloud & AI OPM guidance cut to 14% from 18.4%. SOX now -40% off June peak. SK Hynix -11%, Samsung -10% overnight. RBC desk reports 70:30 better for sales with semis down 7.9% and AI basket down 6.4%.

bullets.title: WDAY: F3Q Beat but F4Q/FY28 Guidance Disappoints; Subscription Growth Decelerates Third Straight Quarter
bullets.body: WDAY F3Q revenue $2.71B (+0.7% beat), EPS $2.82 (+2.9% beat), AI ARR +130% y/y. But F4Q subscription revenue guidance of $2.60B was 0.4% below consensus (10% growth vs. 12.8% prior), and FY27 subscription revenue raised only +0.1%; FY28 growth outlook ~11%. cRPO expected 10-11% vs. prior 11-12% range. Stock -10% pre-market. GS and RBC cut PTs.

bullets.title: SNOW: Pre-Q Preview Bullish — JPM Expects 40%+ Product Revenue Growth, Beat-and-Raise
bullets.body: JPM Overweight on SNOW heading into F3Q27 earnings; partner checks show Cortex/CoCo driving 10-30% incremental credit consumption, practice growth stable at ~20% y/y, and AI workloads at ~40-45% of practice. Expects product revenue to beat $1,591M consensus and F4Q27 guide to frame ~40% exit growth supporting positive FY28 revisions above 30% sell-side consensus. DADCO also models ~28-29% Atlas growth vs +26% guidance.

bullets.title: SHOP: JPM Raises PT to $200; Enterprise Demand Accelerating with ~14 New Logo Wins in Q3
bullets.body: JPM reiterates Overweight on SHOP with $200 PT (based on ~23x 2028E gross profit of $11.1B). Enterprise client wins accelerated to ~14 in Q3 from ~10 in Q2; enterprise estimated to grow to ~7% of 2027E revenue. BFCM GMV growth expected 30%+ y/y after +27% in 2025. Luxury brand adoption (Givenchy, Chaumet/LVMH) strengthening positioning.

bullets.title: PINS: Up 9.5% — Exec Comp Change-of-Control Provisions Signal M&A Prep; New MSFT Ad Deal
bullets.body: PINS board amended change-of-control severance provisions for executives, raising M&A likelihood. New Microsoft advertising integration also announced. JPM speculates potential acquirers include SHOP, AMZN, MSFT, ETSY, or private equity. RBC maintains Outperform at $65 PT (cut from $90).

bullets.title: HPE: Beats Q4 but Cloud & AI Margin Compression Crushes Stock -16%; FY27 Margins Guided Lower
bullets.body: HPE Q4 EPS 83c vs. 74c consensus, revenue $16B vs. $15.26B; but Q1 FY27 OPM guidance cut to 14% from 18.4% and FY27 AI networking orders imply Q4 at ~$1.2B was peak. Q1 guidance midpoint of 71c missed 72c consensus. GS raised PT to $75 and maintained Buy; Citi raised PT to $29, maintained Neutral. Stock -16%, worst day since 2020.

bullets.title: COIN/HOOD: Wedbush Initiates Both at Outperform — $127 PT on COIN, $80 PT on HOOD
bullets.body: Wedbush initiated Coinbase at Outperform with $127 PT (24% upside vs. current ~$102) and Robinhood at Outperform with $80 PT (22% upside vs. ~$65.65), citing crypto/fintech recovery. Both PTs are well below FactSet consensus averages ($189 for COIN, $124.94 for HOOD). Bitcoin down 1.6% to $58,601 in pre-market.

bullets.title: MDB: Improving Sentiment Pre-Earnings; DADCO Models ~28-29% Atlas Growth vs. +26% Guide
bullets.body: MDB earnings due Dec 1 (consensus EPS $1.61, revenue $762.5M). DADCO expects ~28-29% Y/Y Atlas growth vs. +26% guidance, with investor sentiment improving. RBC maintains Outperform at $465 PT heading into F3Q27 results with CEO transition in focus.

bullets.title: MRVL/CRM: Upcoming Earnings Catalysts — Dec 1-2 Reports
bullets.body: MRVL reports Dec 1 at 4:30pm ET (consensus EPS $1.10, revenue $3.15B); CRM reports Dec 2 at 5:00pm ET (consensus EPS $3.45, revenue $11.46B). Semiconductor short interest in MRVL up 25% in early November per RBC, adding event risk context.

bullets.title: AI Bubble Bear Case: Noble Shorts IREN/CRWV; Token Spend Plateauing; Capex Slowdown Risk
bullets.body: George Noble (Market Voices) says the AI investment bubble is unwinding, discloses shorts in IREN and CRWV citing persistent credit weakness, and warns of potential Oracle bankruptcy. Separately, buy-side dinner notes token spend has leveled off and Jevons Paradox appears broken for AI — combined with collapsed token pricing and contracted compute, implies far less AI capex/chip spending than priced. Burden of proof shifting to AI vendors proving sustainable models.

bullets.title: ADBE (via ADSK proxy): UBS Maintains Buy at $325 PT; Low-Teens Growth Durable Through FY28
bullets.body: UBS Buy on ADSK at $325 PT; Q3 C/C organic adj. revenue growth ~11.7%, billings ~11.5%, consistent with Q2. FY27 FCF guide reiterated at $2,750M. MaintainX acquisition adds modest incremental interest in 1H FY28. Watch point: 4Q EBA renewal cohort execution and Western Europe softness. Citi neutral, cuts PT to $260 on Q4 organic growth slowdown and FY28 uncertainty.

bullets.title: META: Muse-AMZN Deal Discussions Ongoing; Walmart Integration Live for Black Friday
bullets.body: META and Amazon are negotiating integration of Meta's Muse AI shopping agent to bypass Amazon's existing blockade; talks focus on search results, advertising revenue split, and product quality. Separately, Walmart has already integrated Muse for Black Friday deals. META stock down 1.7% pre-market amid broader tech risk-off.

bullets.title: MSFT: Withdrawing from Data Center Deals in UK and Texas Amid Sector Scrutiny
bullets.body: MSFT is reportedly withdrawing from data center deals in the UK and Texas as global banks and lenders scrutinize data center operators and AI chip customers. GPU pricing falling ~7% as Asia operators shift excess capacity to US/European markets; multiple APAC data center IPOs delayed.

bullets.title: AAPL: 2027 iPhone Shipment Target Cut 5.6% to 220M Units on High Chip Costs
bullets.body: Per Jiemian, Apple has cut its 2027 smartphone shipment target by 5.6% year-over-year to 220M units due to high chip (memory/DRAM) costs. Peers cutting more sharply: Xiaomi -25%, Vivo -29%, Lenovo -20%, OPPO -14%.

bullets.title: GEV: JPM Sees Supply Tightness Supporting Margins on Data Center Power Demand Acceleration
bullets.body: JPM raises 2028 datacenter power installed base forecast to 303GW (38% CAGR 2025-28) driven by higher GPU/ASIC shipments. GEV supply tightness viewed as favorable for margins; NVT best positioned in US data center on liquid cooling exposure. Data center power demand expected to accelerate through 2028 per GS with 36GW annual capacity in 2028.

bullets.title: W (Wayfair): MS Overweight, $155 PT; Mizuho Also Bullish on Market Share and Margin Path
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintains Overweight on Wayfair with $155 PT, citing rewards/agentic commerce/logistics driving customer loyalty and high-single-digit comp momentum expected through fall. Mizuho also maintains Outperform, noting management confident in >100bps spread growth vs. market in furniture/home goods. Dec 8 MS CTO event on agentic commerce.

bullets.title: HIMS: ROTH Launching GLP-1 Employer Coverage Survey; Key Readthrough for 2027 Access
bullets.body: ROTH QSG deploying proprietary survey of 100-150 U.S. employer benefits decision-makers on sponsored GLP-1 coverage for 2027 benefits, with explicit read-throughs for HIMS (along with LLY, NVO, CVS, CI, UNH). Survey will assess approved coverage, diabetes vs. obesity eligibility, utilization controls, and cash-pay alternatives.

bullets.title: TSLA/SPCX: RBC Notes Potential Merger Announcement Early 2027; May Not Require Significant Premium
bullets.body: RBC notes a TSLA/SPCX merger could be announced as early as 1Q27 and that the deal structure might not require a significant premium to TSLA holders, keeping the transaction more shareholder-friendly than feared.
